Class Plot3D

java.lang.Object
com.eco.bio7.spatial.Plot3D
public class Plot3D extends Object
A simple API to create 3D plots in the 3D view (the space view) without OpenGL code: the data of one or more plot layers (scatter, line, filled line, surface, wireframe, bars, contour, pie and the charts line graph, box plot, violin plot, histogram, area, radar, rose and treemap, see PlotCharts) with a title, axis titles, log axes, number formats, a legend and a color bar. The data is fitted into the plot box (the axis numbers show the values of the data) and the plot is drawn in the 3D view (also without a running model). A plot can be exported to an HTML page with WebGL (see exportHtml).

Example (Java or Groovy): 

double[] x = ..., y = ..., z = ...;
new Plot3D().title("Measurements").axisTitles("Length [cm]", "Width [cm]", "Height [cm]")
                .add(Plot3D.scatter(x, y, z).label("Species A"))
                .show();

new Plot3D().title("z = sin(x) cos(y)").add(Plot3D.surface(xs, ys, zGrid).colorMap(PlotLegend.VIRIDIS))
                .colorBarTitle("z").show();

Plot3D.clear(); // removes the plot
The texts can contain the math markup of the plot view (x^2, x^{-0.5}, N_0).

    Exports the plot for Blender: the glTF file (see exportGltf) and a Python script with the same name (*.py) which imports the file in Blender and adds the title, the axis titles and the numbers as text objects, a camera and the lights (in Blender: Scripting - Open - Run Script).
    void
    exportGltf(String file)
    Exports the plot to a glTF binary file (*.glb), e.g., for Blender (File - Import - glTF 2.0): an object for each layer (named after the label) with the vertex colors, the points as spheres, the lines as tubes and the box, the grids and the axes as an object "Frame" (not for a pie chart).
    void
    exportHtml(String file)
    Exports the plot to an HTML page with WebGL (a single file without dependencies): the plot can be rotated with the mouse and zoomed with the mouse wheel in a web browser.

    • show

      public Plot3D show()
      Displays the plot in the 3D view (opens the 3D perspective if necessary). The plot replaces a displayed plot.
      Returns:
      the plot

    • update

      public Plot3D update()
      Updates the displayed plot with the current layers (e.g., in each step of a simulation, also from the OpenGL thread of a model): the plot is computed again and the 3D view displays it in the next frame. The camera, the font sizes and the view are kept (the 3D view is not opened or brought to the front, see show). Fixed ranges (xRange, yRange, zRange) avoid that the axes change with the data.
      Returns:
      the plot

    • clear

      public static void clear()
      Removes the displayed plot from the 3D view (and the title, the axes and the legends of the plot).

    • exportGltf

      public void exportGltf(String file) throws IOException
      Exports the plot to a glTF binary file (*.glb), e.g., for Blender (File - Import - glTF 2.0): an object for each layer (named after the label) with the vertex colors, the points as spheres, the lines as tubes and the box, the grids and the axes as an object "Frame" (not for a pie chart). The texts are not part of the file (see exportBlender).
      Parameters:
      file - the glTF file (*.glb)
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be written

    • exportBlender

      public String exportBlender(String file) throws IOException
      Exports the plot for Blender: the glTF file (see exportGltf) and a Python script with the same name (*.py) which imports the file in Blender and adds the title, the axis titles and the numbers as text objects, a camera and the lights (in Blender: Scripting - Open - Run Script).
      Parameters:
      file - the glTF file (*.glb), the script is written next to it
      Returns:
      the path of the Python script
      Throws:
      IOException - if a file cannot be written
